title: Undo a bad update with time travel

ticket.subject: Every customer is in France now
body: Someone ran `UPDATE customers SET country = 'FR'` on the lake without a WHERE. The five customers we added
just before are real and must stay.
`customers` is a DuckLake table: every change is a snapshot, and older snapshots can still be read. Please
put the table back as it was right before the bad update, **as a new change** on top of the history (the
auditors want to see the mistake and its fix). Don't drop or replace the table.
Work in `fix.sql` (DuckDB SQL; the lab attaches the lake as `lake` and makes it the default database).

acceptance.text: customers holds exactly the rows it had before the bad update

checks.fail: The table is not back to its state before the update.

acceptance.text: The fix is a new snapshot; the history (including the mistake) is still readable

checks.query: SELECT count(*) FROM customers AT (VERSION => 3) WHERE country <> 'FR'
checks.fail: The snapshot of the mistake was changed.

hints: `SELECT snapshot_id, changes FROM lake.snapshots()` lists the history. Which snapshot is the last good one?
`SELECT * FROM customers AT (VERSION => n)` reads the table as it was at snapshot n.
Replace the rows inside one transaction: `BEGIN; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers SELECT * FROM customers AT (VERSION => n); COMMIT;`
